title: Determinant constants and Euler characteristic
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, put $q=p^a$, and set
$k_0=\Fq$; let $k=\Fbar$ be the
fixed algebraic closure of $k_0$.
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and fix an
indeterminate $T$. For $P(T)=\sum_r c_rT^r\in\mathbf Z[T]$, write
$P^{(\ell)}(T)=\sum_r(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r$ for coefficientwise extension.
Let
$X_0/k_0$ be smooth,
proper, and geometrically connected of pure dimension
$d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $F$ be
geometric Frobenius. For each integer $i$
with $0\leq i\leq2d$, let

$$
V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql),\qquad
F_{i,\ell}=F\vert_{V_{i,\ell}},\qquad
P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell}).
$$

These data form the
smooth-proper
cohomological family, where $H^i(X,\Ql)$ is
ordinary cohomology. Let
$P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be an
integral Frobenius factor
with $P_i(0)=1$ and $P_i^{(\ell)}(T)=P_{i,\ell}(T)$, and define the
Betti number
$b_i=\deg P_i=\dim_{\Ql}V_{i,\ell}$.
For a polynomial $P(T)=\sum_{r\geq0}c_rT^r$, with coefficients
$c_r$ indexed by integers $r\geq0$, and an integer $m\geq0$, write
$[T^m]P(T)=c_m$ for its coefficient of $T^m$.
For $0\leq i\leq2d$, set

$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z\setminus\{0\}.
$$

The image of $D_i$ in $\Ql$ is
$\det(F_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\Ql))$. Define

$$
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i.
$$

Define also the alternating determinant scalar

$$
\Delta=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}\in\mathbf Q^\times.
$$

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against its source (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-def-roots/def-weil-determinant-constants.md); it is verbatim and has no slopmaster2 copy, so it was kept. The definition is built from the global finite-field datum, the geometric hypotheses, the geometric Frobenius on cohomology, ordinary cohomology, the smooth-proper cohomological family, the integral Frobenius factor and the Betti numbers (the seven imported stmt_deps, all confirmed as used), plus three notions the text used without a node: the operator $F$ on $H^i(X,\Ql)$, which is def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius (added; def-weil-frobenius-detailed only fixes the geometric convention); the coefficient $[T^m]P$ of a polynomial, defined inline, now the Mathlib leaf def-weil-polynomial-coefficient (Polynomial.coeff); and the coefficientwise extension $P^{(\ell)}$, defined inline here and in 25 other nodes, now the Mathlib leaf def-weil-coefficientwise-extension (Polynomial.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ_[ℓ])). The text asserts $D_i\in\mathbf Z\setminus\{0\}$ and $\Delta\in\mathbf Q^\times$, which the definition of $\Delta$ needs; that proof is the new leaf lem-weil-leading-coefficient-nonzero (Polynomial.leadingCoeff_ne_zero), added as a statement dependency. The two remaining remarks in the text, that $b_i=\dim_{\Ql}V_{i,\ell}$ (this is prop-weil-betti-comparison) and that the image of $D_i$ in $\Ql$ is $\det(F_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\Ql))$ (stated by no node; the imported proofs downstream use $D_i$ through the reciprocal-root factorization instead), are claims, not notions, and were left in the text and reported. Mathlib was searched for the node itself: no match; $D_i$, $\chi$ and $\Delta$ are each one line over Mathlib once the inputs are stated.
